newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Aug 15.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Winebox findings put leadership on edge: Wide differences emerged in the coalition leadership on Thursday after the Winebox commission of inquiry cleared those involved in the supposed tax scams. Page 1.

Henry may seek compensation: Former Inland Revenue Department head David Henry is to seek legal advice about claiming compensation for the damage caused to his career as a consultant by allegations ruled baseless. Page 1.

Anderton files second breach of privilege claim on Kopu: Alliance leader Jim Anderton filed a letter with Speaker Doug Kidd on Thursday alleging a second breach of parliamentary privilege, an Alliance spokesman said. Page 2.

Parliament passes bill removing super surcharge: Parliament rubber-stamped legislation removing the superannuation surcharge on Thursday amid testy debate over which political party was most tainted by the much-criticised measure. Page 2.

BIL, Camerlin set up joint venture: Brierley Investments and its 20 percent shareholder Camerlin have set up a US$150 million (NZ$234 million) joint venture targeting listed companies in Asia. Page 13.

Record profit and rights issue from St Lukes: Shopping centre owner St Lukes made a record $31.1 million after-tax profit in the year to June and announced a $90 million rights issues on Thursday. Page 13.

Farmers Deka posts small increase in sales: Retailer Farmers Deka has recorded an increase in same-store sales for the year to August 3 of 1.4 percent to $775.3 million in sluggish retail conditions. Page 13.
Telecom fails to gain injunction: Telecom New Zealand has failed to gain an interim injunction to stop a rival from publishing a business directory in Wellington. Page 13.
THE PRESS

Defiant Peters fends off barrage: Treasurer Winston Peters fought off a barrage of attacks -- including several calls to resign -- after the damning Winebox Inquiry report was released on Thursday. Page 1.
PM's days 'numbered': Prime Minister Jim Bolger's days were numbered now that he had aligned himself with a "thoroughly discredited individual", backbencher John Banks said on Thursday night. Page 3.

'Man of integrity' would apologise, says Henry: If Winston Peters was a "man of integrity", he would apologise to Inland Revenue staff and their families for what they have suffered, former Inland Revenue Commissioner David Henry said on Thursday. Page 3.
Lee 'feared assault' by Kopu: Alliance co-deputy leader Sandra Lee said on Thursday she feared an abusive Alamein Kopu was going to assault her in her office. Page 5.
NZ Petroleum issue for native forests: New Zealand Petroleum on Thursday announced a convertible note rights issue as it branches out into forestry. Page 13.
Solid start by Colonial: Australasian insurer Colonial has posted a A$118 million (NZ$138.2 million) net profit for its first half ended June 30. Page 14.
Telstra looks for more: Telstra New Zealand is spending another $30 million on its business this year and is confident of a ten percent market share by 2000. Page 14.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Damning report turns up heat on the coalition: A humiliated Winston Peters has placed himself on a collision course with his National coalition partner by threatening legal action to overturn Thursday's highly embarrassing findings of the winebox inquiry.
Tax reform overshadows corporate celebrations: Corporate tax dodgers and their lawyers face a harsher future under law changes recommended by the winebox commission of inquiry.
Tax experts relieved at acceptance of reforms: Winebox commissioner Sir Ronald Davison has come out with only a minor list of firm recommendations for further reform of the tax laws.
Super savings targer may drop: The savings targets for compulsory superannuation would be significantly lowered under planned changes to the tax laws.
Bank to chase slice of HP pie: The Bank of New Zealand has launched an assault on an estimated $2 billion market for personal loans and hire purchase.
